seg: 593P Vigabatrin Improves Rigidity in Stiff-Person Syndrome (SPS) Rocco Liguori, R. Medori, and L. Marchello, Bologna, Italy; L. Grimaldi, Milan, Italy; E. Lugaresi and P. Montagna, Bologna, Italy

Objectiue. To study the efficacy of vigabatrin on muscle stiffness in SPS (Moersch-Woltmann syndrome). Background. Vigabatrin irreversibly i n h i b i t s gammaaminobutyric acid (GABA) transaminase and is mostly used for complex partial seizures. SPS is characterized by progressive rigidity and painful muscle spasms due to loss of GABAergic inhibition on alpha motorneurons. Autoantibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) may be found. Design. A woman presented with SPS confirmed by EMG studies and high t i t e r of autoantibodies against GAD. The patient was bedridden and unable to walk even with high doses of diazepam (60 mg/d) and baclofen (125 mg/d). To this treatment, we added vigabatrin 3 grid in two doses. Results. Vigabatrin 3 gr/d resulted i n marked improvement of rigidity in the legs and reduction of muscle spasms. Within 10 days, the patient could flex hips and knees and walk with assistance. However, withdrawal of diazepam resulted in reappearance of muscle spasms. The patient was thus continued on vigabatrin 3 gr/d and diazepam 30 mg/d and has remained well during 8 mos of follow-up. Conclusions. Vigabatrin decreases rigidity of SPS and allows lower doses of diazepam to control muscle spasms.
